comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target is the generic bachelor "Literatuur en Samenleving", which the current official Teaching and Examination Regulations (OER 2026-2027) and programme pages confirm is delivered through two formal tracks: "Literature and Society: English" and "Creatief Schrijven Nederlands" (Creative Writing Dutch). Neither track name is named by the normalized target itself, so the neutral route-selection rule applies. "Literature and Society: English" is selected as the more broadly representative route because its own name and academic core (literary theory, genre analysis, literature-and-society content, a general academic core of academic training, methods, philosophical training, history of science and academic English) directly continue the parent programme's stated identity, whereas "Creatief Schrijven Nederlands" is explicitly marketed as "the first Dutch bachelor's degree in creative writing", a materially more specialised professional-writing variant. The OER's own Article 11.1 confirms a shared academic-core structure across both tracks (academic training; methods and techniques; philosophical training; "Wetenschapsgeschiedenis: Cultural History"; and a track-specific academic-language component), and Article 11.5 confirms the exact EC value of each track's final independent-research component (12 EC for the English-track Bachelor Thesis; 9+3 EC for the Dutch-track thesis and colloquium). The OER states the general structural rules governing the reconstructed 180-EC pathway: an academic core of at least 24 EC, a major of at least 90 EC, a free-choice/profiling space of at least 30 EC in the first semester of Year 3, and standard course units of 6 EC or a multiple thereof, with 3 EC (or a multiple) as the only documented exception. The current official annual-plan appendix (Bijlage 1 Programmaschema, OER 2026-2027) names every compulsory Year 1-3 unit of the selected route by title and period, and the OER defers the exact per-unit EC table for those named units to the course catalogue (studiegids.vu.nl) rather than reprinting it in the OER body. Individual current-year course-catalogue pages under that same official study-guide path (using the programme's own vakcodes, e.g. L_ELBALESAV1/AV2, L_ELBALES1xx-3xx, L_ELBALESSCR) were checked directly and confirm the EC value of the great majority of Year 1 and all Year 2-3 named units, uniformly following the OER's own 6-EC default with a 3-EC exception limited to the two paired "Academic Skills" methods units; the two paired "Academic Orientation" units and the "English Language Test" are confirmed/inferred as 0-EC compulsory pass/fail compliance items (Academic Orientation 1 and 2 were individually confirmed at 0 EC and, carrying no EC weight, are not listed as separate credit-bearing components below; the English Language Test, together with "Academic English Grammar" and "Academic English Writing" and "Literature, Culture and Society", were not individually reachable through the course catalogue within this session. The English Language Test is a compulsory pass/fail entry check carrying no EC weight and is likewise not listed as a separate component. "Academic English Grammar" (3 EC), "Academic English Writing" (3 EC) and "Literature, Culture and Society" (6 EC) are assigned the closing values needed for Year 1's credit-bearing components to reach exactly 60 EC using only the OER's own permitted 3/6-EC unit sizes; this is a closure derived strictly from officially confirmed unit sizes and the officially confirmed Year 1 course list, not an invented curricular fact. The "Pronunciation Presentation" item appearing in the annual plan is an alternative assessment format inside one Year 2 unit rather than a separate credit-bearing unit and is not listed as a separate component. Of the route's two mutually exclusive Year 3 specialisations ("Literature in a Changing World" and "Literature in a Visual Culture"), "Literature in a Changing World" is instantiated because it is the specialisation directly named by a Stable study direction programme-interest row for this exact target (row 4826), while "Literature in a Visual Culture" is equally attested (row 4827) but only one can define the single coherent reconstructed pathway. The Year 3 first-semester free-choice/profiling space (at least 30 EC, Article 12.1) is preserved generically at its full 30 EC rather than filled with an invented minor package.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: This route replaces 9 of the 24 courses used in the closest-match programme (GOSPHIL214, MCCCOMM311, MCCHEAM112, MCCHEAM212, MCCHEAM312, MCCLITR312, MCCMEDI112, MCCMEDI212, MCCMEDI311) with 9 different courses centred on practice-based writing, rhetoric and contemporary media production (MCCLITR112, MCCLITR212, MCCMEDI211, MCCCOMM111, MCCCOMM213, MCCCOMM312, GOSPHIL311, GOSPHIL313, GOSSOCI214). alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest-match programme covers the core literary-analytical field, its two direct changing-world and visual-culture stable study directions (the changing-world specialisation is instantiated; visual-culture is substantively covered by the same close-reading and text-screen core, since both name the same normalized target's Year 3 specialisation choice), and the general literature-and-society direct interests. The Dutch creative-writing track's four stable study directions plus the direct creative-writing/individual-voice interest are evidenced by a genuinely different, coherent 24-course programme organised around practice-based writing and media production rather than literary-critical analysis, differing from the closest match by 9 of 24 courses. Every generator-eligible interest row is now owned by one of these two programmes, leaving no remaining coherent, evidence-backed direction for a third alternative: UCR offers no further dedicated creative-writing, journalism or publishing infrastructure beyond what the second alternative already uses, so a third programme could only be built by re-shuffling courses already scheduled in the first two programmes rather than from new evidence; production stops at two.

notes.text: Literature and Society: English requires a compulsory academic core (academic skills, orientation and academic-English modules), ten-plus named literary and cultural units across Year 1-2, a Year 3 changing-world or visual-culture specialisation, and a compulsory 12-EC Bachelor Thesis. UCR's selected programmes can combine a comparable range of literary, media, historical and philosophical courses, but UCR offers no dedicated British-literature, global-English/sociolinguistics, publishing-industry or transatlantic-travel-writing course, and no compulsory bachelor's thesis; UCR's standardized Optional independent research element is offered instead of a required thesis.

Creatief Schrijven Nederlands trains sustained creative-writing craft (fiction, poetry, scriptwriting, podcasting) as a dedicated skills sequence across three years. UCR offers no dedicated creative-writing workshop sequence; the second UCR alternative instead approaches creative and persuasive writing through UCR's rhetoric, communication and media-production courses, which train related craft and performance skills rather than reproducing a full creative-writing curriculum.
